title: November 13 — Korva, Astra's KORVA / WORLDS and Entrain's live cochlea
summary: A practical/audio-visualization branch. July's already-curated Entrain demonstrates microphone-driven Stuart–Landau resonators and measured entrainment, not audio-style transfer. November's Korva uses period-selecting delay rings as auxiliary tokens for a small transformer on synthetic rhythm tasks. The upgraded MusicVisualizer1 / KORVA / WORLDS (Astra) reuses the Korva model and offers six GPU/Canvas artistic audio-reactive scenes. Only Korva-to-MusicVisualizer1 is a direct code-inheritance claim; other visual analogies are inspirations, not imported neural or physical systems. The new visualizer directory is a navigation aid rather than a scientific ranking.

nodes.claim: A rhythm-memory organ of 52 fixed delay rings (laps 13–64 ticks) selects three low-surprise periods and feeds their expectations to a tiny two-layer, two-head transformer.
nodes.survived: The README reports F1 0.91 on synthetic periodic rhythm bands for a window-12 transformer with ring organ, compared with 0.00 without organ under the same short training budget; random lap selection yields 0.13. The browser page demonstrates local files, demo songs and keyboard tapping.
nodes.killed: Period-selection comb filters and memory-enhanced attention have prior art. The task favors long-period memory, the baselines are training-limited, and the real-song example scores only 0.27 rhythm-band F1. Gating writes did not improve the tested synthetic result. The original Korva page has no microphone input.
nodes.era: November 13: sound as measured dynamics and art

nodes.claim: Astra's KORVA / WORLDS update to MusicVisualizer1: six sound-reactive browser worlds (Crystal Cathedral, Fourier Bloom, Tidal Silk, Phase Loom, Resonant Cortex and Event Horizon), with local file/mic/tab audio, captures and unchanged Korva organ/transformer code.
nodes.survived: The README documents direct browser playback, real-time FFT-based audio response, WebGL-1 ray-marched/Canvas fallback scenes, six selectable worlds, memory-ring overlays, PNG/WebM export and original synthesized demo music. Tests are described for shader/offscreen behavior and JS controls.
nodes.killed: Artistic worlds are not implementations of Moon's light-transport model, CrystalMoon's voxel simulation or RCNet inference. Phase Loom is a delay embedding, not proof of a reconstructed attractor. Korva's synthetic-rhythm scores do not validate next-beat accuracy on arbitrary real songs; no universal FPS guarantee.

edges.why: MusicVisualizer1 explicitly reuses Korva's 52-ring organ, trained tiny transformer and unchanged korva-engine.js/weights.js, while adding a new renderer and live audio front end.

The KORVA / WORLDS README explicitly credits the earlier phase-space visualization idea; Phase Loom renders delay-coordinate trajectories from actual samples. This is inspiration, not a claim that VST code is imported.
The new Fourier Bloom world explicitly credits FourierFlower as harmonic-flower visual inspiration; new procedural rendering code is original to MusicVisualizer1.

motifs.title: Listening organ, resonator and visual world are different machines
motifs.description: Entrain displays physically modeled oscillator response and measured phase-locking; Korva reads ring-period memories into transformer attention; MusicVisualizer1 uses audio features to animate original artwork while retaining Korva as a separate inspectable organ. Their shared word 'resonance' does not turn them into the same algorithm. This group is a visual-demo directory, not a novelty or empirical-performance claim.
